title: Field engagement: model profiles and decision memo
content:
Background:

This memo captures our recommended model profiles, quantization strategy, and prompt/pipeline tuning plan for the upcoming field engagement with NovaPay (card processing startup). The engagement objective is a 2-week trial to validate throughput, latency, and end-to-end accuracy for the customer’s customer-support summarization and classification flow.

Goals and success criteria (customer-facing):
- Latency: 95th pctile <= 450ms for single-turn summarize+classify (target region: us-west).
- Cost: target per-1000-reqs token cost <= 40% of current prod baseline (customer-provided).
- Accuracy: summary ROUGE-L >= baseline + no more than 3% drop in category F1.
- Reliability: graceful fallback to smaller model if dedicated capacity temporarily saturated.

Customer constraints / notes:
- Data: transcripts are short (avg 120 tokens) but contain multi-lingual snippets and CommonFormatting quirks (timestamps, code blocks).
- Security: must run in customer-dedicated pool (no network egress for transcripts).
- Throughput: expected steady-state 20 qps, with 1.5x peak bursts.
- Budget: prefers smaller instances; willing to trade some accuracy for predictable latency/cost.

Experiment scope and quick wins:
- Focus on two model families and three quant profiles: (A) 13B dense (high quality), (B) 7B dense (latency-focused).
- Quant profiles: FP16 baseline, 8-bit PTQ (int8), 4-bit QAT-lite (PTQ with per-channel scaling recommended).
- Quick win: enable prefix KV caching for repeated similar queries (customer uses repeated template prompts).

Candidate model matrix (shortlisted):
- Model-A: Large-13B-Instruct (13B) -- baseline quality.
- Model-B: Mistral-7B-Instruct (7B) -- higher throughput per GPU.
- Model-C: L2-7B-approx (7B) -- lower mem footprint, slightly weaker long-form coherence.

Quantization strategies we will explore:
1) FP16 (no quant) - establish quality & baseline perf.
2) 8-bit PTQ (symmetric int8, per-tensor) - expect ~1.6x throughput improvement; verify hallucination delta.
3) 4-bit PTQ (GEMM-friendly, per-channel scales) - aim for ~2.5-3x throughput, validate severe degradation risks on classification heads.
4) 4-bit QAT-lite (calibration + small fine-tune on customer prompt set) - only if 4-bit PTQ shows >5% accuracy drop.

Prompt/pipeline tuning plan:
- Canonical prompt templates: create short and long templates for summarization + classification. Keep instruction tokens minimal to reduce cost.
- Two-stage pipeline: (1) lightweight extractor prompt to normalize/strip timestamps and code blocks, (2) summarizer + classifier prompt run as single batch where possible.
- System messages: pin temperature=0.0 for classifiers; 0.2 for summaries. Limit max_new_tokens = 150 for summaries.
- Use sampling-free decoding (greedy / beam-size 1) for determinism/cost.

Evaluation matrix (per experiment):
- Metrics collected: latency p50/p95, tokens per call, summary ROUGE-L, classification F1, GPU mem footprint, effective throughput (qps), cost estimate per 1k requests.
- Datasets: use 300 representative customer transcripts (sanitized) + 1k synthetic edge cases (multi-lingual snippets, truncated turns).
- Runs: each model/quant/prompt pair gets 3 trial runs at steady state and a 5-minute burst to capture autoscaling behavior.

Recommended starting configs (priority order):
1) Mistral-7B-Instruct @ FP16; prefix KV caching enabled; two-stage pipeline (extractor + summarizer/classifier). Baseline: validate latency and quality.
2) Mistral-7B-Instruct @ 8-bit PTQ; run same prompts and compare ROUGE/F1. If delta < 2%, mark as candidate for production.
3) Large-13B-Instruct @ FP16; only used for an A/B sample (10% traffic) to measure upper-bound quality.
4) If cost remains high and accuracy acceptable, try Mistral-7B @ 4-bit PTQ + calibration; if >5% accuracy drop, stop and consider QAT-lite.

Operational notes for Dedicated pool setup:
- Machine sizing: start with gpus that provide ~40GB GPU RAM to allow FP16 inference on 13B for the A/B test. For 7B variants, 24–32GB GPUs suffice.
- Autoscaling policy: maintain min capacity for 25 qps headroom; rapid scale-up on queue depth > 50 for >30s (to handle bursts).
- Fallback routing: create a policy to route to a lower-cost model variant when queueing time > 200ms or when instance health metrics indicate memory pressure.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: 4-bit PTQ causes classification head drift for category labels. Mitigation: hold classification head on FP16 (hybrid quant) or run classifier on 13B sample path for edge cases.
- Risk: preprocessing extractor misses timestamp variants leading to hallucinations. Mitigation: add small deterministic regex-normalizer step in preprocessor and evaluate on synthetic edgecases.
- Risk: customer data patterns unseen in our calibration set. Mitigation: include customer-provided examples in calibration/fine-tune loop (consent confirmed).

Instrumentation & observability to enable during trial:
- Per-route latency and token breakdown (extractor vs model vs postprocessing).
- Quality drift alerts: daily batch eval on held-out 100 examples; threshold triggers rollback of quant profile.
- Cost per 1k requests and effective GPU utilization dashboard.

Decision checkpoints and gating:
- Gate 1 (day 2): FP16 7B baseline must meet latency p95 target. If not, reduce max_new_tokens or move to higher GPU spec.
- Gate 2 (day 6): 8-bit PTQ for 7B must show accuracy drop <= 2% vs FP16 and cost improved by >=25% to proceed to wider traffic.
- Gate 3 (end of trial): If combined metrics meet latency/cost and accuracy goals, propose Dedicated contract sizing (commit tiers) and rollout plan.

Deliverables for the trial:
- Trial runbook with commands to switch quant profile, rollout percentages, and rollback steps.
- Benchmark report: perf + quality tables for every model/quant/prompt pair.
- A short customer-facing one-pager summarizing recommendations and cost/latency tradeoffs.

Open questions / TODOs (owners):
- [Miguel] Confirm GPU SKUs available in customer-dedicated pool and whether 40GB nodes are allowed (due EOD 11/13).
- [Sara] Sanitize and deliver the 300 representative transcripts and label schema (due 11/08).
- [Priya] Create calibration micro-dataset (200 examples) for 4-bit experiments (due 11/09).
- Decide whether to enable quantization-aware training (QAT-lite) for the classifier head if hybrid approach needed.

Notes to se-team: keep experiment artifacts reproducible: store exact model hashes, quantization scripts, and prompt templates in the linked GH PR. Prefer deterministic seeds for sampling experiments.

Appendix: quick command snippets
- Start FP16 run (example): ./run_benchmark --model mistral-7b --precision fp16 --prompt-template templates/summarize_v1.txt --dataset nova-300.json
- Convert PTQ 8-bit (example): python tools/quantize.py --model-path models/mistral-7b --out models/mistral-7b-int8 --scheme symmetric --per_channel false
- Calibration run (4-bit): python tools/quantize.py --calibrate --bits 4 --per_channel true --calib-data calibration/nova-calib-200.json

If anyone on the thread has objections to model ordering or thinks we should prioritize L2-13B as the baseline instead of 7B for quality reasons, flag now. Otherwise we’ll run the fastest-to-iterate path (7B FP16 -> 7B int8 -> 13B sample path).

End of memo.
